# Battle of Acroënus (1146)

* Capture & Sack of Philomelion
| combatant1        = Byzantine Empire
| combatant2        = Sultanate of Rum
| commander1        = Manuel I Komnenos
| commander2        = Unknown
| strength1         = Unknown
| strength2         = Unknown
}}
The Battle of Acroënus (modern-day Afyonkarahisar) was part of a punitive expedition to counter Turkish raids on Byzantine frontiers that took place during the eventual failed Expedition to Iconium Which was Personally led by Emperor Manuel I Komnenos against the Sultanate of Rum who aimed to punish Seljuk incursions against Mesud I, forces Under Manuel soon routed the Turks. The Battle paved way for Manuel to advance towards the fortified town of Philomelion which he captured & Destroyed after Removing the remaining christian population.
